details: Uranium-238 decay series (4n+2 series): U-238 (t½=4.468×10⁹yr) → Th-234 (24.1d) → Pa-234m (1.17min) → U-234 (245,500yr) → Th-230 (75,400yr) → Ra-226 (1600yr) → Rn-222 (3.82d) → Po-218 (3.05min) → Pb-214 (26.8min) → Bi-214 (19.7min) → Po-214 (164µs) → Pb-210 (22.3yr) → Bi-210 (5.01d) → Po-210 (138.4d) → Pb-206 (STABLE); alpha emitters in chain: U-238; U-234; Th-230; Ra-226; Rn-222; Po-218; Po-214; Po-210 = 8 alpha decays; beta emitters: Th-234; Pa-234m; Pb-214; Bi-214; Pb-210; Bi-210; total energy release: ~51.7 MeV per U-238 → Pb-206 chain; secular equilibrium: in undisturbed ore: all members at same activity as U-238
chernobyl_relevance: Chernobyl relevance of U-238 series: RBMK fuel was low-enriched UO₂ (2.8% U-235; 97.2% U-238); fuel age at accident: 2-4 years (short compared to secular equilibrium 3-5 half-lives of Th-234 = ~120d; Th-230 = 377,000yr); freshly produced fuel: NOT in equilibrium above Th-230 (too short); U-234 and Th-230 and Ra-226 and Rn-222 NOT present in new fuel in secular equilibrium amounts; Chernobyl soil U-238: natural background + depleted U from fuel debris; U-238 in CEZ = natural background (3 ppm granite basement) plus very small reactor contribution (mostly trapped in fuel matrix)
source: Bateman 1910; Evans 1955 The Atomic Nucleus; NNDC; natural_background_radiation_REAL.csv; quantum_nuclear_physics_fundamentals_REAL.csv

details: Uranium-235 decay series (4n+3 series; actinium series): U-235 (t½=703.8×10⁶yr) → Th-231 (25.52hr) → Pa-231 (32,760yr) → Ac-227 (21.77yr) → Th-227 (18.68d) → Ra-223 (11.43d) → Rn-219 (3.96s) → Po-215 (1.78ms) → Pb-211 (36.1min) → Bi-211 (2.14min) → Tl-207 (4.77min) → Pb-207 (STABLE); also branching through At-215 and Po-211; 7 alpha decays; contribution to natural background: U-235 only 0.72% of natural U; therefore U-235 series contributes less to background than U-238 series (lower abundance); Pa-231 (32,760yr) = important long-lived intermediate: relevant for nuclear non-proliferation (Pa-233 + n → U-233 = weapons material in Th fuel cycle)
chernobyl_relevance: U-235 in Chernobyl context: RBMK fuel initially 2.8% U-235; after 15,000 MWd/tHM burnup: depleted to ~0.6-1.0% U-235; U-235 fission = primary energy source (>90% of neutron-induced fissions); Pu-239 contributes 20-30% of fissions at end of life; U-235 decay series in spent fuel: same as natural series but U-235 concentration is 'enriched' (above natural 0.72%); fission products completely dominate radioactivity in fresh spent fuel (factor 10^6 more active than decay series); after >1000yr: fission products decayed; decay series again dominant; Chernobyl fuel debris in soil: U-235 series present at above-background levels within 10km of reactor

details: Thorium-232 decay series (4n series; thorium series): Th-232 (t½=14.05×10⁹yr) → Ra-228 (5.75yr) → Ac-228 (6.15hr) → Th-228 (1.912yr) → Ra-224 (3.66d) → Rn-220 (55.6s) → Po-216 (0.145s) → Pb-212 (10.64hr) → Bi-212 (60.55min; 64% β→Po-212→Pb-208; 36% α→Tl-208→Pb-208) → Pb-208 (STABLE); 6 alpha decays; Ra-228 and Ac-228 = highest-dose members in normal terrestrial environments; Th-232 crustal abundance: 10.5 mg/kg (4× uranium); therefore Th-232 series contributes significantly to natural gamma background; Tl-208 emits 2614 keV gamma (highest energy natural gamma = used for neutron-deficient isotope separation monitoring); Rn-220 (thoron t½=56s): much shorter than Rn-222 (3.82d) → limited health impact vs Rn-222
chernobyl_relevance: Th-232 in Chernobyl context: Th-232 is not present in RBMK fuel (no thorium fuel cycle); Th-230 = U-238 series daughter (not Th-232 series); CONFUSION POINT: Th-230 and Th-232 are different isotopes from different series; natural background from Th-232 series in CEZ granite/sandy soils: ~0.03-0.05 µSv/hr from Th-232 + daughters + K-40 combined = this is the BASELINE dose rate; above this baseline: Chernobyl contamination adds additional dose rate; current CEZ outer zones: Th-232 natural background may be comparable to or exceed remaining Chernobyl dose rate contribution in some low-contamination areas
source: NNDC; natural_background_radiation_REAL.csv; UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; Firestone 1996

details: Radon-222 health physics: Rn-222 (t½=3.82d; alpha emitter → Po-218); primary health concern: short-lived progeny inhaled and depositing in lung; critical progeny: Po-218 (t½=3.05min; α 6.003 MeV) + Pb-214 (t½=26.8min; β) + Bi-214 (t½=19.7min; β + 609 keV γ) + Po-214 (t½=164µs; α 7.687 MeV); alpha dose from Po-218 and Po-214 to bronchial epithelium → lung cancer; equilibrium factor F = ratio (actual progeny concentration) / (secular equilibrium with Rn); indoor F = 0.3-0.4 (not all progeny reach equilibrium due to plate-out on surfaces); lung dose coefficient: 9 mSv/(mJ·h·m⁻³) for equilibrium Rn; effective dose: 3-10 mSv/yr at 100 Bq/m³ indoor (WHO guideline); WHO 100 Bq/m³ reference level; USEPA action level 148 Bq/m³ (4 pCi/L)
chernobyl_relevance: Radon in context of nuclear accidents: natural Rn-222 doses (1-10 mSv/yr thyroid equivalent: NO; Rn doses LUNG specifically); in CEZ: natural Rn emanation from U-238 in sandy soils; Rn dose adds to overall radiation exposure; Rn dose from Pu-239 NOT significantly increased (Pu-239 → Am-241 → Np-237 → Pa-233 → U-233 → Th-229 → Ra-225 → Ac-225... different series NOT leading to Rn-222 in significant quantities); Chernobyl: Rn contribution to liquidator dose = negligible compared to external gamma; to current CEZ visitor dose = negligible; to self-settler annual dose: ~1-2 mSv/yr (same as global average) = comparable to Chernobyl external gamma contribution of ~1-5 mSv/yr in mid-contamination zones
source: WHO 2009 Handbook on Indoor Radon; ICRP 115 2010; natural_background_radiation_REAL.csv; radiation_dose_limits_REAL.csv

details: Secular equilibrium: condition where daughter nuclide activity equals parent activity; condition: t½_parent >> t½_daughter; establishment time: 5-10 × t½_daughter; examples: (1) U-238 (4.468×10⁹yr) with Th-234 (24.1d): equilibrium established in ~120 days; (2) Ra-226 (1600yr) with Rn-222 (3.82d): equilibrium in ~20 days; (3) Pb-210 (22.3yr) with Po-210 (138.4d): equilibrium in ~2 years; broken equilibrium: geological processes separate parents from daughters; ore processing (uranium extraction) leaves daughters behind; mining tailings = Ra-226, Rn-222, Pb-210, Po-210 with no parent U-238 → decay continues; Ba-137m secular equilibrium with Cs-137: t½(Ba-137m)=2.55min << t½(Cs-137)=30.17yr → immediate equilibrium → ALL 662 keV gamma from Ba-137m detected = 85% of Cs-137 decay events
chernobyl_relevance: Chernobyl Cs-137 secular equilibrium: Ba-137m (t½=2.55min) is always in secular equilibrium with Cs-137 → 85% of decays produce 662 keV gamma; this is why Cs-137 is so easily detected (its daughter is always present); Am-241 secular equilibrium with Np-237 (t½=2.144×10⁶yr): NOT established yet (Am-241 t½=432yr; only 40yr elapsed → far from equilibrium); Am-241 is STILL GROWING from Pu-241 (see am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv) and NOT yet decaying to Np-237 significantly; radioactive_decay_chains_REAL.csv has full list

details: Potassium-40 (K-40): natural radioactive isotope; abundance 0.0117% of natural K; t½=1.248×10⁹yr; decay modes: 89.28% β⁻ (E_max=1311 keV) → Ca-40 (stable); 10.72% electron capture → Ar-40 + 1460 keV gamma; specific activity K-40 = 3.14×10⁴ Bq/g K; total body K = 140 g (70 kg adult; 2 g/kg); body K-40 activity = 140 g × 0.0117% × 3.14×10⁴ = 4,405 Bq; annual effective dose from K-40: ~0.17 mSv/yr (internal); bone marrow dose from K-40 beta: ~0.12 mGy/yr; contribution to natural background: 10-15% of total 2.4 mSv/yr global average; daily dietary K = 3.5-4.7 g/day; K-40 intake = constant (body maintains homeostasis; excess K excreted)
chernobyl_relevance: K-40 context for Chernobyl: body K-40 activity (4400 Bq) > typical liquidator total Cs-137 body burden (1000-10,000 Bq); but Cs-137 dose coefficient 1.3×10⁻⁸ Sv/Bq vs K-40 integral dose ~0.17 mSv/yr per 4400 Bq = 3.9×10⁻⁸ mSv/Bq/yr → K-40 and Cs-137 produce comparable doses per Bq; difference: K-40 is CONTROLLED by homeostasis (body maintains fixed K pool); Cs-137 is ADDITIONAL external burden (body has no regulatory mechanism for Cs); therefore Cs-137 adds proportionally to baseline K-40 dose; K-40 in food: 100-200 Bq/kg in most foods (grain; meat; milk); banana = ~15 Bq K-40 per banana (famous comparison)
source: UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; ICRP 30; natural_background_radiation_REAL.csv; chernobyl_key_numbers_reference_REAL.csv

details: Pb-210/Po-210 dietary pathway: Pb-210 (t½=22.3yr) and Po-210 (t½=138.4d) = U-238 series members; accumulated in marine food chain (especially shellfish, fish liver); mechanism: Rn-222 from ocean → decays to Pb-210 → adsorbs to marine particles → sinks to sediment → remobilized by benthic organisms → concentrates in seafood; Po-210 in seafood: 10-100 Bq/kg wet weight; annual dietary Pb-210 dose: ~0.15 mSv/yr; for high seafood consumers (Arctic indigenous; fish-eating cultures): up to 1-2 mSv/yr; Pb-210 in Arctic: caribou/reindeer consume lichen (exceptional Pb-210 accumulator: Fv=100-1000); Sami reindeer herders: Pb-210 + Po-210 in reindeer liver = most significant natural internal dose pathway
chernobyl_relevance: Context: natural Pb-210/Po-210 doses from seafood can EXCEED typical Chernobyl contamination doses for populations without CEZ food pathway; for reindeer herders: Chernobyl Cs-137 in reindeer (100,000 Bq/kg) adds to existing Pb-210/Po-210 burden; Chernobyl impacted all natural dose pathways; in CEZ: Black Sea fish Pb-210 pathway exists but normal marine fish consumption contributes natural Pb-210/Po-210 at levels comparable to or exceeding residual Chernobyl Cs-137 doses; example: annual dose from Po-210 in shellfish = ~0.1 mSv; vs Chernobyl Cs-137 in non-CEZ food = <0.001 mSv/yr (2026)
source: ICRP 30; Radford 1977 NEJM (Pb-210/Po-210 in tobacco); UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; baltic_sea_contamination_REAL.csv; black_sea_contamination_REAL.csv

details: Natural uranium in soils: global average U-238: 25-60 Bq/kg (depends on rock type: granite 100-200 Bq/kg; sandstone 10-40 Bq/kg; basalt 10-20 Bq/kg); CEZ geology: mainly sandy Quaternary sediments over granite basement; surface soil U-238: ~20-40 Bq/kg natural; Chernobyl-deposited U: from fuel fragments = very small addition to natural U (<0.1% increase in typical CEZ soils outside immediate NPP vicinity); thorium Th-232: global average 45 Bq/kg; K-40: 400-800 Bq/kg; comparison with Cs-137 contamination: in low contamination outer CEZ zones (37 kBq/m²): Cs-137 ~460 Bq/kg (40 cm soil layer) = comparable to natural K-40; in hot spot areas 4000 kBq/m²: Cs-137 ~50,000 Bq/kg = 100× natural K-40 = clearly anomalous
chernobyl_relevance: Total natural gamma dose rate in Central Europe: ~0.07-0.15 µSv/hr from K-40 + U-238 series + Th-232 series; current CEZ dose rates (Chernobyl city): 0.209 µSv/hr = 1.4-3× natural background = LOW; current Pripyat: 4.932 µSv/hr = 33-70× natural background = ELEVATED but not immediately dangerous (1yr continuous = 43 mSv = above 1 mSv public limit but below occupational 20 mSv); context: dose rate at major airports from cosmic rays + naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM) in construction materials: 0.1-0.5 µSv/hr; current Chernobyl city = comparable to some natural high-background areas
source: UNSCEAR 2000 Annex B; modern_monitoring_REAL.csv; natural_background_radiation_REAL.csv; chernobyl_key_numbers_reference_REAL.csv
